provider: Oxen.ai (Oxen Hub — dataset versioning for ML)

free_tier.stated: Explorer (free forever): 50 GB data storage + 50 GB data transfer, unlimited public repos with unlimited collaborators, 5 private repos (max 3 collaborators). Hacker $30/mo: 100 GB storage / 100 GB transfer. Pro $60/mo: 500 GB / 500 GB.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Hard-capped at 50 GB of data transfer per month on the free tier. Transfer allowances are exhausted quickly under continuous data retrieval.

tooling: Genuine: `oxen` CLI (oxen add/commit/push/pull, merkle-tree diffing), Python SDK, and a documented REST API. The oxen-server is open source and self-hostable (Oxen positions itself as 'git for data'). This is a real product with a real client, not a wrapper.
chaining: 50 GB x N free accounts, but the 50 GB/month transfer cap applies per account too, so chaining accounts multiplies egress but not storage usefulness. 10 TiB would need 205 accounts.

limits.value: transfer, unlimited public repos with unlimited collaborators, 5 private repos

limits_note: 50 GB storage, 50 GB/month transfer, 5 private repos. No per-file cap published. Public repos are unlimited in COUNT, which is the only multiplier. But the 50 GB is account-level, so repo count does not add bytes.
reliability_note: Mature, funded, stable. Data is content-addressed and versioned, so no silent expiry. The API host api.oxen.ai did not resolve from this network, which suggests the documented API endpoint has moved or is geo-restricted.

extras.limits_verbatim: 50 GB storage, 50 GB/month transfer, 5 private repos. No per-file cap published. Public repos are unlimited in COUNT, which is the only multiplier — but the 50 GB is account-level, so repo count does not add bytes.
extras.egress_verbatim: Hard-capped rather than metered: 50 GB of data transfer per month on the free tier. That is the binding constraint for the 500 GB-1 TiB/day serving workload — you would exhaust a month of transfer in about an hour and a half.

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
